parsed.elsewhere_quote: Let $P$ be the union of all terminal members. It is a finite set of primes. If a prime $p$ occurs in any $C\in\mathcal C$, Lemma 2 supplies a terminal $D\in\mathcal C$ containing $p$. Therefore every prime occurring in any member of $\mathcal C$ belongs to $P$.
parsed.explanation: The objection is arithmetically right: $D\setminus\{p\}$ has $|D|-1$ primes, so the correct bound is $2^{|D|-1}\le w(D\setminus\{p\})<a_1$, not $2^{|D|}$. But the conclusion drawn is only that $|D|$ is bounded: $2^{|D|-1}<a_1$ gives $|D|<1+\log_2 a_1\le a_1$ for $a_1\ge 2$, so "$|D|\le a_1$" and the appeal to Lemma 1 (finitely many members of bounded size) stand. Hence the finiteness of terminal members, of $P$, and of $\mathcal C$ — the write-up's substitute for large-prime erasure — is established; only the exponent in the display is a misprint, fixable by one symbol.
